title: Compute auxiliary functions f and g
action:
Select at least 8 parameter combinations covering σ=2‑15 Å, t=10,30 Å, ξ=10,30 Å. For each combination, evaluate the dimensionless double series f and g defined by:
f = (16/(π⁴σ)) Σ_{k,l≥0} {1 − exp(−Pₖₗ t) + exp(−Pₖₗ(t−2σ)) − exp(−Pₖₗ 2σ)} / {Pₖₗ (2k+1)² (2l+1)²},
g = (16/(π⁴σ)) Σ_{k,l≥0} {t exp(−Pₖₗ t) − (t−2σ) exp(−Pₖₗ(t−2σ)) + 2σ exp(−Pₖₗ 2σ)} / {(2k+1)² (2l+1)²},
with Pₖₗ = (π/ξ) √((2k+1)² + (2l+1)²). Sum over k,l until convergence (e.g., k,l up to ~2000). Save the results to f_g.csv with columns: sigma, t, xi, f, g.
description: Computes auxiliary functions f and g for each parameter point as intermediate evidence.
output_schema: CSV with columns: sigma (float), t (float), xi (float), f (float), g (float)

title: Compute magnetoelastic tensor components and anisotropy constant
action:
Using the previously computed f and g, obtain the dimensionless surface magnetoelastic tensor components (normalized by 2πMs²) and surface anisotropy constant:
Bs_3333 = −(1−g) σ/2,
Bs_3311 = −(1−2f+g) σ/2,
Bs_1111 = −(π σ t)/(4 ξ),
Bs_1122 =  (π σ t)/(4 ξ),
Ks = −(3/4) σ (1−f).
Write a CSV file with columns: sigma, t, xi, f, g, Bs_3333, Bs_3311, Bs_1111, Bs_1122, Ks. All quantities are dimensionless; use at least 6 decimal places.
description: Computes all roughness‑induced surface magnetoelastic tensor components and the surface anisotropy constant.
output_schema: CSV with columns: sigma (float), t (float), xi (float), f (float), g (float), Bs_3333 (float), Bs_3311 (float), Bs_1111 (float), Bs_1122 (float), Ks (float)
